examples.en: My friends snickered behind me and looked at me.
I giggled to myself while reading a comic book.
If you snicker during class, the teacher will scold you.
The two are whispering and giggling.
What's so funny that you're snickering like that?
The sound of giggling could be heard all the way to the hallway.

explain: 혼자 재미있어하거나 남을 놀리듯이 목구멍에서 새어 나오는 소리로 웃는 모습이에요. 때로는 놀리거나 비웃는 느낌도 있어요. 밝고 시원하게 크게 웃는 '깔깔거리다'와 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes laughing in a sniggering way, with sounds leaking out from the throat, either amused to yourself or at someone's expense. Sometimes it suggests teasing or mocking. It feels different from '깔깔거리다', which is a bright, hearty laugh.

en: to be taciturn; to be reticent

examples.ko: 동생이 하루 종일 뚱해서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: My younger brother has been sulky all day and isn't talking.

examples.ko: 왜 그렇게 뚱한 얼굴로 앉아 있어요?
examples.en: Why are you sitting there with such a sulky face?
He answered sullenly, as if he were upset.
The child who got scolded is sulking.

examples.ko: 표정이 뚱하고 말이 없어서 걱정이 됐어요.
examples.en: He looked sulky and silent, so I was worried.
My friend was late, so I was in a sulky mood.

explain: '뚱뚱하다'와는 전혀 다른 말이에요. 못마땅하거나 기분이 안 좋아서 말없이 퉁명스러운 표정이나 태도를 보일 때 써요. '뚱한 표정', '뚱하게 앉아 있다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is completely different from '뚱뚱하다' (fat). It describes a sulky, silent look or attitude when someone is displeased or in a bad mood. Common patterns are '뚱한 표정' and '뚱하게 앉아 있다'.

en: to be calm; to be unmoved

examples.en: Even after hearing the news of the breakup, he seemed unfazed.
The indifferent way you answered hurt me a little.
I cried at first, but now I feel calm about it.
He had a deadpan look even after receiving a present.

examples.ko: 무덤덤하다고 해서 아무 감정이 없는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because someone seems unmoved doesn't mean they have no feelings.

examples.ko: 아버지는 무덤덤해 보여도 속으로는 걱정이 많으세요.
examples.en: My father looks unbothered, but inside he worries a lot.

explain: 겉으로 감정을 잘 드러내지 않거나 별로 마음이 흔들리지 않는 모습에 쓰는 일상적인 말이에요. 속으로는 감정이 있을 수도 있어서 '무감동하다'보다 부드러워요. 말투나 태도가 퉁명스러운 '무뚝뚝하다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is an everyday word for someone who doesn't show feelings outwardly or isn't much shaken. They may still have feelings inside, so it is softer than '무감동하다'. It differs from '무뚝뚝하다', which describes a curt, blunt manner of speaking or acting.

en: suddenly (in a burst of anger or uproar)

examples.ko: 사장님이 거짓말을 알고 발칵 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: The boss found out about the lie and suddenly flew into a rage.

examples.ko: 시험지가 바뀌었다는 소식에 학교가 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
examples.en: The school was thrown into an uproar at the news that the exam papers had been mixed up.

examples.ko: 형이 발칵 소리를 질러서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My older brother suddenly yelled, and it startled me.

examples.ko: 친구가 별것 아닌 일로 발칵 짜증을 냈어요.
examples.en: My friend suddenly got irritated over something trivial.
The door suddenly flew open and everyone was startled.

examples.ko: 회사 비밀이 새어 나가자 사무실이 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
examples.en: When the company secret leaked out, the office was in an uproar.

explain: 갑자기 화를 내거나 소란이 일어날 때 써요. '발칵 화내다', '발칵 뒤집히다'처럼 짝으로 많이 나와요. 비슷한 '왈칵'은 눈물이나 감정이 갑자기 쏟아질 때 써요.

phrases.example: 아이가 사라졌다는 소식에 온 동네가 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
phrases.en: At the news that the child had disappeared, the whole neighborhood was in an uproar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 뒤집히는 게 아니라, 어떤 일 때문에 사람들이 놀라고 크게 술렁이는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean something is flipped over; it means people are shocked and a place is thrown into a big stir over some event.

explain_en: It is used when anger or a commotion breaks out suddenly. It often appears in pairs like '발칵 화내다' and '발칵 뒤집히다'. The similar '왈칵' is used when tears or emotions suddenly burst out.

examples.en: My younger sibling sulked because they couldn't get the toy.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 말에 삐쳐서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: My friend is sulking over what I said and won't talk to me.

examples.ko: 별것도 아닌 일로 자꾸 삐치지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't keep sulking over trivial things.

examples.ko: 남자친구가 삐친 것 같은데 어떻게 풀어 줘야 할까요?
examples.en: My boyfriend seems sulky. How should I make it up to him?

examples.ko: 아이가 삐치면 한참 동안 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: When my child sulks, he doesn't talk for quite a while.
He's really sulking, so apologize first.

explain: 크게 화내는 것보다 서운해서 말을 안 하거나 토라지는 가벼운 감정이에요. 친구, 연인, 가족처럼 가까운 사이에서 많이 쓰고, 말할 때는 '삐지다'라고도 자주 해요. 비슷한 '토라지다'와 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a mild feeling of being hurt and going quiet, not full-blown anger. It is used among close people like friends, partners and family, and in speech people often say '삐지다' too. '토라지다' is a close synonym.

en: oh no; oh my gosh; oh my goodness

examples.en: Oh no, I left my wallet at home.
Oh no, today was the deadline!

examples.ko: 아뿔싸! 하고 외쳤을 때는 이미 늦었어요.
examples.en: By the time I cried out 'Oh no!', it was already too late.
Oh no, I forgot to bring my phone charger.
Oh no, I got on the bus going the wrong way.

examples.ko: 문을 닫고 나서야 아뿔싸, 열쇠가 안에 있다는 걸 알았어요.
examples.en: Only after closing the door did I realize, oh no, the key was inside.

explain: 실수나 잘못을 방금 깨닫고 후회할 때 혼잣말처럼 해요. 말투가 조금 예스럽고 이야기 속 느낌이 있어서, 가볍게 말할 때는 '아차'나 '앗'도 써요.
explain_en: You say it like a mutter the moment you realize a mistake and regret it. It sounds a bit old-fashioned and storylike, so in casual talk people also use '아차' or '앗'.

examples.en: Whoa, I almost missed my step.
Oof, I didn't know it was this heavy.
Oops, I spilled the coffee!
Whoa, you startle me when you come out so suddenly!

examples.ko: 어이쿠, 정말 미안해요, 앞을 못 봤어요.
examples.en: Oops, I'm so sorry, I didn't see you.
Goodness, it's already this late.

explain: 깜짝 놀랐을 때, 실수했을 때, 몸이 아프거나 힘들 때 나오는 소리예요. 비슷한 소리로 '아이쿠', '어이구'가 있어요. 말투가 조금 정겹고 가벼워서 일상 대화에서 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: This is the sound people make when startled, when they make a mistake, or when something hurts or is tiring. Similar sounds are '아이쿠' and '어이구'. The tone is a little warm and light, so it fits everyday conversation.

examples.en: I can't stand bugs.
My younger sibling can't stand spicy food.
My father really hates being late.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 신발이 젖는 건 질색이에요.
examples.en: I hate it when my shoes get wet on rainy days.
I hate cleaning, but I have to do it today.
My friend can't stand lies, so my friend is always honest.

explain: '싫어하다'보다 훨씬 강하게, 보기만 해도 몸이 움츠러들 정도로 싫을 때 써요. 보통 '~라면 질색이다'나 '~(은/는) 질색이다'처럼 말해요. 가볍게 말하는 구어에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '싫어하다': you recoil just at the thought of something. People usually say '~라면 질색이다' or '~(은/는) 질색이다'. It comes up often in casual speech.

en: to complain; to grumble; to growl

examples.en: My younger brother grumbles that there are no side dishes.
The child whined for me to buy a toy.
Please don't keep complaining that it's hard.
If I whine to my mom, I feel a bit better.
He worked while grumbling that his pay was low.
The way she whined like a spoiled child was cute.

explain: '불평하다'와 달리, 가까운 사람에게 어리광을 부리듯 불만을 늘어놓는 느낌이에요. 실제 대화에서는 '투정을 부리다'라는 말도 많이 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '불평하다' (to complain), it feels like airing grievances to someone close in a childish, spoiled way. In real conversation people also often say '투정을 부리다'.

en: gasp; gasping; whoa (sound of sudden shock)

examples.en: Gasp, I didn't bring my wallet!

examples.ko: 뒤에서 소리가 나서 헉 하고 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A sound came from behind and I gasped in shock.
Whoa, it's already ten o'clock?

examples.ko: 계단을 뛰어 올라오느라 헉 숨이 찼어요.
examples.en: I ran up the stairs and was out of breath.
I gasped when I saw the price.

examples.ko: 친구가 헉 하는 소리를 내며 뒤로 물러섰어요.
examples.en: My friend made a gasping sound and stepped back.

explain: 갑자기 놀라거나 숨이 찰 때 나오는 소리예요. 문자나 메신저에서 '헉'이라고만 보내도 놀랐다는 뜻이 돼요. 비슷한 '헐'은 어이없거나 놀랄 때, '아'는 깨달았을 때 써서 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It is the sound you make when startled or out of breath. In texts a bare 헉 means you are shocked. 헐 is similar but leans toward disbelief, and 아 is for sudden understanding, so the feelings differ.
